title: 输入法组字确认与聊天发送的区别
evidence_scope: Source-derived event-sequence explanation and original unexecuted game-chat design example. No browser, IME, Unity or SDL execution.

sources.title: UI Events
supports: The draft ending sequence labels exit keydown as composing and subsequent keyup as not composing.
Composition end covers completion and cancellation, not a game message-send operation.
limitations: Working draft, not a measured browser implementation or universal native ordering.

sources.title: Input Events Level 2
supports: Editing intention and composition are distinct from application-level message submission.
limitations: Section7 orders compositionupdate before beforeinput/input; UI Events section3.6.6 describes a differing order. This reader does not resolve the discrepancy or build on that ordering.

sources.title: HTML Standard — Implicit submission
sources.version: Living Standard; page showed updated2026-10-30 when read
supports: Implicit submission can activate a default submit button under the specified support and button conditions.
limitations: Does not say every IME confirmation triggers submission. Application must inspect actual control/form pathways, no browser run.

sources.title: Keyboard support
sources.version: Branch1.11 page identified as1.11.2 when read
supports: Text input uses text callbacks rather than manually assembled key presses.
onIMECompositionChange describes composition text; imeSelected reports enabled IME processing, not by itself an active composition detector.
limitations: Mutable version branch, not pinned implementation. No Unity callback ordering or actual UI behavior measured.

original_example: Fictional chat recipient and draft, candidate confirmation must not be reinterpreted as a fresh send from the release half of the same action. Actual routing depends on the selected component.
